note: Load statements that only register callbacks and run nothing until the server is up. A statement that runs while a file loads normally pins everything it can reach, the functions it hands over included, because nothing can tell whether the callee calls them at once. A statement listed here is one where a person read every callee and found that it only keeps what it is handed: for it, the tool follows only what the statement calls itself. An entry names the statement by its first line, the files that were read (callees, each with the SHA-256 of the text read, line endings as LF) and the reason in one sentence. The tool checks what it can and drops the entry when a check fails: a callee whose text changed has to be read again; every call the statement makes, every call it hands a function to and every module it loads in place has to lead to a file in callees (calls to Node's own modules and to globals aside), so a statement that calls a function of its own file cannot be listed. What the tool cannot check is the reason itself: add an entry only after reading the callee and confirming it stores the callback and calls nothing at load. When in doubt, leave the statement blocked.

server/server.js.reason: createLayersEdit keeps broadcast, onEnd and onOff in its closure and returns an object of functions; it calls none of them and starts no timer until set() is called.

createScreenMenu declares its own state and functions and returns them; host, broadcast, panel, run, failed, capturing and holding are first called by open(), close() and the other functions it returns.

createCapabilities keeps the object it is handed and returns probes, run and seedKeys without calling any of it; platformDeps and createNotificationOpener build closures over what they are handed, and createStartAppIds keeps its reader for the first tap; power/index.js is only loaded here, as it is today, and is handed nothing.
setIgnoreSource stores the function in a variable and clears a cached list; the function is first called by isIgnoredProc, when a process is checked.
createLyricsTranslator calls complete and onError only inside request(), which translate() reaches; at creation it builds a cache from its own functions and passes neither callback on.
createSdkAi calls complete, blocker and onError only inside ask(); at creation it works out a file path and returns ask and usageToday.
createWidgetKeys calls layers only inside read() and onChange only from press, release and a peek timer that press starts; at creation it makes empty sets and returns its functions.

createDarwinMedia and createLinuxMedia keep onChange in a variable and return available, start, stop, info and command; onChange is called only from handleLine, retire and command, which run once start() has spawned the reader, and createLinuxMpris, which createLinuxMedia hands it to, calls it only from its poll tick.
createMediaSender returns one async function and does nothing else; request, tell, press and listResting are called only when that function is.

createSituations makes empty sets and returns tick, hidden and needs; layers, every reader, isOwnApp, onChange, onPlan, onFacts and warn are first called from tick() or needs(); power/index.js is named inside the battery reader and loaded when that reader first runs, as it is today.

createRegistry keeps the object it is handed, reads its platform property and returns run; everything else in it is the two functions run and runDeckState, so nothing of the object is called before run() is.

createDeckShortcutRunner and createDeckSoundPlayer make empty sets and maps and return their functions; readConfigs, steps, run, broadcast, serverFirst, resolveFile, ffplay and spawn are first called by press, pressKey, handOff or play; deck-actions.js is only asked for its triggerSteps function and is handed nothing.
createDeckPress declares placed, read, press and accept and returns the last three; layers.get, layers.update, readConfigs and runner are first used when one of them is called.
